title: Arisa
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Tomboyish Tsubasa believes her twin Arisa has a perfect school life until Arisa attempts suicide and falls into a coma. Tsubasa poses as Arisa at her middle school and finds a class in thrall to a hidden 'King' who grants wishes during 'King Time', setting classmates against each other. The shoujo mystery builds to the King's unmasking and his past.
life_message: A life of honest courage that refuses to hand one's will to a manipulator, even for granted wishes.

content.note: Attempted murder and harm engineered by the King (MU categories); ANN describes psychological rather than physical violence (to verify).
Cult-like class worship of the King; ANN calls King Time 'chilling' and faces 'truly scary'; AniList Cult 96%, Psychological genre.
Teen romance; Arisa's boyfriend is fooled by the twin swap (ANN).
Arisa's suicide attempt drives the plot (AniList and Kodansha blurb; MU Attempted Suicide); bullying (MU, AniList 88%); ANN notes Arisa's Stockholm-like attachment at the end.
Wish-granting cell-phone 'King' and class groupthink could be imitated as a game (to verify).
Cell phones central as plot device only.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Tsubasa answers threats personally, but the plot resolves through truth rather than revenge.

Order vs freedom.evidence: The story critiques the class's ordered obedience to the King.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Twin loyalty drives every risk Tsubasa takes.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Hidden hierarchy of the King is shown as false authority.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Secular school setting; no religious frame beyond cult-like worship.

folkways.japan: Class-group cohesion and fear of standing out, strong in Japanese middle schools, are what the King exploits; the story uses them as setting.

delivery.evidence: ANN reviewers praise the chilling cult mystery and call the uncomfortable ending realistic; none call it preachy.
delivery.note: The danger of groupthink is carried by the mystery's twists and Tsubasa's choices rather than stated speeches.

winners_losers: Tsubasa saves her sister and herself; the King is exposed, though ANN notes Arisa stays attached to him, so the ending is not clean.
